commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: doctor

Done. All 29 errors in `server/mcp/tool-executor.ts` are fixed.

**Verification** — `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`:
- `server/mcp/tool-executor.ts`: **0 errors** (was 29)
- Repo-wide error count 781 → 752 (exactly −29); a sorted set-diff of before/after shows **zero new errors** in any file.

**What was actually wrong, and the fixes:**

1. **Untyped JSON-RPC args reaching typed parameters** (~15 errors, TS2345/TS2322/TS2538/TS2339). `ToolArgs` is `Record<string, unknown>`, so `args.foo || 'x'` widens to `{}`. Added small narrowing helpers at the trust boundary — `asString`, `asOptionalString`, `asStringArray`, `asRecord` (via an `isRecord` type guard) — and used them in `generateArtifact`, `checkContentEnforcement`, `governedGenerate`, the narrative-coherence handlers, and `auditDigestibility`. Each mirrors the old `|| fallback` semantics. `runEscalation` now coerces with `Number(...) || 30`.
2. **`Surface` (line 250, TS2345).** Added a type-only import of `Surface` from `./fail-closed-gate` (keeps the module's lazy `await import`) plus a `SURFACE_BY_NAME` lookup and `asSurface()` — a cast-free map from caller string to the union, falling back to `'general'` exactly as before.
3. **`json(...)` didn't exist** (11 errors, TS2304/TS2552) — the surface-governance handlers were calling a helper that was never defined. Replaced with the file's own `mcpText()`, which produces the `MCPContent` these handlers declare.
4. **`f.file` on `SurfaceFinding`** (TS2339) — the interface has `location`, not `file`; the projection now emits `location: f.location`.
5. **Control-plane gate** (TS2339/TS2353). `ctx.userId` doesn't exist on `ExecutionContext`; used the trusted identity that does — `ctx.authenticatedTenant?.tenantId || 'mcp-caller'` (unknown ids fall through to the `default` policy, so gating behaviour is unchanged). `surface`/`riskScore` aren't in `EnforceRequest`, so they moved into its `metadata` bag rather than being dropped. `cpResult.blocked` doesn't exist on `EnforceResult` → `!cpResult.allowed`.

Two of these are latent runtime bugs the compiler was flagging, not just type noise: the `json()` calls would have thrown `ReferenceError` on any `surfaceGovernance.*` call, and `cpResult.blocked` was always `undefined`, so the control-plane block branch could never fire in hard/soft mode — it can now.

I attempted to run the four vitest files that reference `tool-executor` as an extra check; the host declined the command, so the compiler result above is the verification that ran. Nothing was committed or pushed.
